precepts.label: Isaiah 1:16-20
precepts.why:
Naaman was told, “Wash, and be clean”, and when he believed and obeyed the word of the prophet, he was clean. Isaiah shows what the true washing is: “Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; Learn to do well”.

Put away the evil of your doings: that's the true washing. Cease to do evil, learn to do well. Action, action, action. Not speak well, do well. “seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.”

“though your sins be as scarlet”, bloodshot red, “they shall be as white as snow”, if you learn to do well. “though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.” But it hangs on obedience: “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword”.

That is Naaman. At first he refused and went away in a rage. When he humbled himself and did according to the saying of the man of God, his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. His belief and his obedience are what made him clean.

precepts.label: Psalms 51:6-7
precepts.why:
Naaman believed that the word of the prophet would heal him if he followed the commandment, going down to the river Jordan and dipping seven times. That belief is what healed him of his leprosy.

David prays the same way: “Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.” Truth in the inward parts is what the Most High desires. Then: “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

The water of the Jordan did not do it by itself; the Jordan was muddy water, and Naaman would rather have had the rivers of Damascus. The word of God is what really cleanses us of our sins. Naaman obeyed the word, and he was made clean, his flesh like the flesh of a little child.

precepts.label: Luke 3:3-4
precepts.why:
We read about Naaman going down into the river Jordan to be cleansed. Luke brings us back to that same river: John “came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins; As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias the prophet, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.”

The baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins, preached about Jordan. Naaman was washed of his leprosy in the Jordan, and John preached the washing away of sins in the same Jordan. Nothing is accidental with the Most High.

It was Christ who healed Naaman, working through Elisha by his spirit. And John in the Jordan was preparing the way of that same Lord.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:13
precepts.why:
“Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.” Christ went unto John the Baptist to be baptized, and in what river? Jordan: the same river that Naaman had to dip in seven times.

Seven represents completion. Naaman dipped seven times in Jordan, completion in the river Jordan, and his flesh came again like the flesh of a little child. The number and the river both point to the same Christ.

Who did the healing for Naaman? Not Elisha on his own. Elisha was working by the spirit of Christ; Christ is the one who did the healing, and he used Elisha as the prophet. So when Christ himself comes to the Jordan, it is the same one who cleansed Naaman there, the one who makes us clean.

precepts.label: Luke 4:25-27
precepts.why:
Christ himself reached back and referenced this exact history. “I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.”

Then the point: “And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.” Of all the lepers, the one cleansed was the one who humbled himself, believed, and went down and dipped seven times according to the saying of the man of God.

And seven also represents complete deliverance. Naaman dipped seven times and was delivered from his leprosy; Christ, the one whose spirit healed him through Elisha, spoke of it himself.

precepts.label: Proverbs 16:18
precepts.why:
The first thing on the list of what the Lord hates is “A proud look.” Proverbs 16 shows where that proud look ends: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.”

Whenever you see somebody fall off, just know there is some form of pride in that man or that woman: something they do not want to address, an inflated ego, disdain, a haughty look, a refusal to come back to God. You might not have seen it. They might have masked it as confidence in your eyes, but God saw it as pride.

Pride is not always loud and in your face. It can be subtle: not asking for help because you do not want to seem weak, holding grudges because you feel justified, saying I am good when you are not, shutting down and thinking you do not need anybody. Pride always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. So when you start feeling yourself too much, puffing your chest out, say, Oh no, I am not trying to fall; let me be humble, let me be loving.

Every kingdom has failed because of pride, even ours. “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride, separating from God to do their own thing, going back to the split under Rehoboam, who would not listen to the elders. Then the southern kingdom: “After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” And the warning to us: “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.”

So the proud look is first on God’s list because it is the start of the fall. God made your eyes, your body and the mind you think with; walking in pride is departing from your maker, and it ends in destruction.

precepts.label: Proverbs 8:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wisdom hath builded her house”. Who is this wisdom? Go back a chapter, where wisdom speaks: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.”

This is going into Christ and wisdom, one and the same, interchangeable. Christ is the ultimate wisdom, the complete wisdom, set up from everlasting before the earth was.

That is why chapter 9 says wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Seven represents completion, and Christ is complete wisdom. The house wisdom built stands on him, the one the Lord possessed in the beginning of his way.

precepts.label: Isaiah 11:1-2
precepts.why:
Wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Let's see who this wisdom pertains to and who had these seven pillars. Isaiah: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That is talking about Christ.

Now count what rests upon him. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: that's one. “the spirit of wisdom”: two. “and understanding”: three. “the spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “the spirit of knowledge”: six. “and of the fear of the Lord”: seven.

Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had. Seven represents completion, so they represent complete spiritual perfection, and that is what Christ operated in. Wisdom's house on seven pillars is Christ, full of the spirit of the Lord in every part.

precepts.label: Sirach 37:16
precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Why? Because of what you were supposed to do first: “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Everything you take on to do, you are supposed to seek counsel. And if you seek counsel and apply it, things are going to go well for you.

But instead of seeking counsel, pride kicks in. I am my own man, I do what I want. A lot of times when brothers have bad dealings with each other, both of them were out of the spirit, because neither one ever asked for counsel: Listen, I want to do this job with so-and-so; what do you think about it?

Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown. I own my own house, I bought it with my own money, I am doing better than you; who are you to counsel me? Then months later, years later, when everything falls apart, now they want counsel. Counsel did not go before that enterprise; pride went before it, and destruction came with it.

You need counsel before, not after. That is why we have to remember the scriptures: blessed is he that readeth, and if we apply what we read, we are going to be all right. Reason and counsel before every action is the cure for the pride that goes before destruction.

thread.text: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

precepts.label: 1 Samuel 2:3
precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

precepts.label: Isaiah 45:15
precepts.why:
“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

precepts.why:
Isaiah calls us “a people laden with iniquity.” Christ answers that very word: “Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” Heavy laden with what? With sin, the iniquity Isaiah just named.

That is why we are in need of a saviour. We read the history of our forefathers in the wilderness: the Most High showed great signs and wonders, and we were still a stiff-necked, hard-headed people. We are “a sinful nation”, “a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters.” We forsake the Lord every time we sin, and we have “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger.” That is why the so-called blacks and Hispanics went into captivity, just as Deuteronomy 28:15 through 68 laid out the curses for breaking the commandments. Many of our brothers and sisters are still going backward, moonwalking away from the Most High. Brothers and sisters, we cannot do it without Christ.

So be honest and sincere, even in prayer. Do not go to the Most High acting righteous when you are full of dead bones, sin and guile. None of us is righteous; we are trying, but there is sin still in us. Open your mouth and confess the things you are battling with.

“and I will give you rest.” That rest is not a good night’s sleep. It is our land, the kingdom of God, rulership for a thousand years under Christ. That is the true rest he is talking about, but we have to come unto him. Now is our time to get our minds right and repent.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 15:24
precepts.why:
Isaiah cries, “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity”. We are laden: like a ladle dipped in soup, we are soaked and drenched with iniquity. A sinful nation means we break God's laws. So what is sin? Ezra answers: “Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! saith the Lord.”

Sin is when we don't keep God's commandments. Brothers, put this in your arsenal. We always go to 1 John 5:3, of course, but we have to understand that it is precept upon precept, and Ezra says the same thing.

And who are the people that were given God's commandments? The twelve tribes of Israel. That is who Isaiah is calling the sinful nation. He was never talking about the Hittites or anybody but the Israelites.

This matters now because wars are here, and it is no time to think you are ready. You may wear your fringes, keep your beard right, keep the Sabbath and put the pork down, but still battle with patience, anger, a brawling spirit, an evil eye, or the weed you won't put down. Woe to them that sin. The whole head is sick: you're sick and I'm sick, and we have to keep getting right.

precepts.label: Psalms 147:19-20
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the sinful nation has “provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger”. To prove which nation that is: “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” Jacob was the forefather of the twelve tribes, and his name later became Israel. The statutes and the judgments were given to the nation of Israel.

“He hath not dealt so with any nation”. So for modern-day Christians to say that God is dealing with all nations and all people, they don't know the Bible.

Then: “and as for his judgments, they have not known them.” The Israelites are the ones that get judged. That is why Black people went into slavery, in the trans-Saharan slave trade and the trans-Atlantic slave trade, and many other times in history we have served our enemies in slavery.

So Isaiah was never talking about anybody but the Israelites. We are the seed of evildoers who call evil good and good evil, led astray by Christian pastors and the leaders in the mosques. From 1865 to 1965 we lived under more overt racism, but we had civility, women had a dress code, and there was an order to talk to a sister. Since 1965 we have gained almost twenty million abortions by Black women alone and the dumbest generation of children with the smartest technology. We provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, and that is why we went into slavery.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 2:1
precepts.why:
“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Before he sets us in our land, he tells the twelve tribes what to do: “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired.” We are the nation not desired, and God is instructing the twelve tribes to gather themselves together, to wake up.

“Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” That decree is the destruction that is prophesied to come. Get yourselves together before destruction comes. Things are moving at a quicker pace, and that is why the Bishop says he loves President Trump: he is forcing prophecies to come to pass and forcing the Israelites to do what the Bible says.

Who gathers? “Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” The meek are humble to God’s word, men and women who do his commandments without making excuses. We cannot gather with camps that say we are not keeping any Sabbath, or that throw you out for wearing fringes with a border of blue.

Then the judgment on the land: “For Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation.” “I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant.” The Palestinians are not just pushed out; according to the Bible they are destroyed. “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”, “for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” That is Israel set in their own land.

precepts.label: Amos 3:3
precepts.why:
“Gather yourselves together” does not mean gather with everybody. “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

You get some morons that say, Let’s join ourselves with the camp that believes John the Baptist was a wicked nigger. You cannot join with that. Let’s join with the camp that believes men do not have to work: get seven women, eight women, and let them work for you. No, we cannot join with that.

Some people are simple, and they ask, Why aren’t y’all all together? This is why. Two cannot walk together unless they are agreed, and the ones who gather are those who “have wrought his judgment”, the meek who do God’s laws, seek righteousness and seek meekness.

So when the Lord will yet choose Israel and set them in their own land, the gathering before the decree is not one of mixed doctrines. It is a gathering of those agreed on God’s commandments.

precepts.label: Amos 9:11
precepts.why:
The Lord “will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land.” Judah shall live on the sea coast, and it gets better: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” And Amos: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old.” The tabernacle of David is the twelve tribes, built again as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name.” There are people calling themselves Jewish today, and Jew comes from Judah, praise of Yahawah; they are not the praise of Yahawah. And people calling themselves Christians, the anointed ones; they are not the anointed ones.

“And I will bring again the captivity of my people of Israel, and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them.” There are waste cities all over there, and after Armageddon there will be more. And we will have servants: that is the strangers joined to the house of Jacob, the heathen round about us as bondmen and bondmaids, when that law goes back in full effect.

“And I will plant them upon their land, and they shall no more be pulled up out of their land which I have given them, saith the Lord thy God.” That is Isaiah 14:1 fulfilled: set in their own land, never pulled out again.

precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. “Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. thread.text: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Isaiah 37:21-38
precepts.why:
Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth, and Assyria is the first king in line. Sennacherib took all the defenced cities of Judah, then sent Rabshakeh, his herald, with big words: “What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?” When Hezekiah's men begged him to speak in the Syrian language so the people on the wall would not hear, he said he was sent to “the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you.” Then he mocked the Lord himself: “Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?” … “that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?” All that pride came out of the king of Assyria's mouth by way of his messenger.

God heard all that smack. “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria: This is the word which the Lord hath spoken concerning him; The virgin, the daughter of Zion, hath despised thee, and laughed thee to scorn; the daughter of Jerusalem hath shaken her head at thee.” She is laughing at this man's tough talk, the way a parent shakes their head when they told you not to do it and are about to whoop your ass. You are not going to one-up God, and that goes for everyone making videos mocking God's prophets. God will one-up you.

“For I will defend this city to save it for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake. Then the angel of the Lord went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.” One of God's angels destroyed 185,000. The sun went down and they were all alive; at the crack of the morning, “they were all dead corpses.” Talking prideful against God, everybody had to die.

But God was hunting Sennacherib himself. “So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.” He thought he got away. Then “as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god”, his own sons “smote him with the sword”, and they escaped into Armenia, and his other son Esarhaddon reigned in his stead and didn't even care.

Pride destroyed the king of Assyria, as “a man’s pride shall bring him low” in Proverbs 29. And it is the same line through every kingdom after him, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America: none is exempt from pride, and none is exempt from God destroying them for it.

thread.label: Isaiah 43:1
thread.text: But now thus saith the Lord that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 6:58
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.” And to redeem us, “I gave Egypt for thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. Since thou wast precious in my sight.” We are precious in his sight because we are the apple of his eye.

Ezra shows what we are to him: “But we thy people, whom thou hast called thy firstborn, thy only begotten, and thy fervent lover, are given into their hands.” We are his fervent lover. We are his bride. We are his wife.

That is why God gave Egypt, Ethiopia and Seba, which is Somalia, for our ransom: to deliver us out of captivity he had to destroy the Egyptian army, and Ethiopia that was a help to them. “therefore will I give men for thee, and people for thy life.” In order for us to be delivered from slavery and captivity, God said, I have to destroy nations for them to release you.

So when Isaiah says “thou art mine”, it is the voice of a husband over his wife. The firstborn, the only begotten, the fervent lover given into the hands of the nations is the one God redeems.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 18:8
precepts.why:
“I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.” Do you think the nations are just going to give his people back? No. Christ comes with armies: “And the armies which were in heaven followed him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.” Wherever the Israelites are, the armies of God will go there and deliver us and destroy those nations.

The Christian mentality wants a white Jesus to come back throwing flowers, and John Hagee says Christ will set his government up to get the Democrats and Republicans in order. Wisdom of Solomon shows what salvation really is: “So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies.” We all want the salvation of the righteous, and we have to accept the destruction of the enemy too. That is what we just read in Isaiah 43.

“For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The same way he punishes our adversaries, he glorifies us. That is the bride of Christ: Christ is coming to get his woman. That is what the whole thing is about.

So the redeeming of Isaiah 43:1, “I have called thee by thy name”, is the calling of Wisdom 18: “us, whom thou hadst called”, glorified by the very judgment that punishes the nations holding us.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 16:14
precepts.why:
“I have redeemed thee.” Jeremiah shows that this redemption will be greater than the first: “Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that it shall no more be said, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.” When he delivered us out of Egypt, he destroyed Egypt, he destroyed Ethiopia and he destroyed Seba, Somalia.

“But, The Lord liveth, that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them.” The land of the north is North America. All the lands whither he had driven them are the Caribbean, Africa, and all the different lands we are scattered in.

“and I will bring them again into their land that I gave unto their fathers.” That is Isaiah 43: “I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west.” We are here in the west, the western hemisphere.

So the redemption promised to Jacob is not the one out of ancient Egypt. It is the deliverance out of the land of the north and every land of our captivity, and it will be so great that the Exodus will no longer be what men speak of.

precepts.label: Romans 8:21
precepts.why:
“Fear not: for I have redeemed thee.” Paul shows what that redemption brings: “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.”

The creature itself is you and me. We shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is talking about us being delivered, not just from this body, but from captivity.

It is the same promise as Jeremiah 16: the Lord that brought up the children of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands whither he had driven them, bringing them again into the land he gave their fathers. Isaiah 43 says he will say to the north, Give up, and bring his sons and daughters from the ends of the earth.

So “I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” ends in liberty: the children of God set free from bondage, the captives delivered in the year of jubilee.

thread.label: Isaiah 49:5-6
thread.text: And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.

precepts.label: Romans 10:14-15
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

We have been sent, throughout the four corners of the earth, and from the beginning, to be saviours. By going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth. “as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

That is why the prophets of God are “glorious in the eyes of the Lord.” There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High God, once he has revealed his son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be athletes, and once Christ was awakened in us we let all that go. None of it compares to what we do now in these last days as watchmen of Israel. This is the true glory, glorious not to man but to God, and our God is our strength to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:21
precepts.why:
Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

precepts.label: Luke 4:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 is fulfilled in Christ, who read it himself: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” The good tidings of Isaiah are the gospel. And the poor are not everybody: “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor are the poor of Zion. You do not even have to go to Isaiah 14; Isaiah 61 itself says it is them that mourn in Zion.

“he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.” We are the captives. How can you read captive and think everybody? Rome was dominating Israel at that time. “and recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind people. “to set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee, and we had better accept that.

Imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors side by side, told we are all the same. It makes no sense. Jake looks over at Esau to see if he is upset, and if master is upset at this reading, he disregards it: black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks, and that is why they do not believe. But Christ read it plainly: he came to proclaim liberty to the captives of Israel, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, bound in these prisons we call America, the Caribbean and whatever lands we are in.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:32
precepts.why:
“the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Christ read it in Luke 4 as “to preach the gospel to the poor.” When it says the poor, who is that? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That is telling you who the poor are: the poor of Zion, the poor of his people. Zion is another name for the Israelites.

And Isaiah 61 itself agrees: he came “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes”. Why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

So the good tidings, the brokenhearted, the captives and them that are bound are not all nations. They are the poor of the Lord’s people, the Israelites in captivity, who shall trust in the Zion the Lord has founded.

precepts.label: Zephaniah 3:19
precepts.why:
When the captives are set free, “ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord”, “For your shame ye shall have double”, and “their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the Lord hath blessed.” No matter where we go on this planet they are going to know our children by name. Today you want to talk to your boss and he turns his back to you; on that day they are going to beg for your attention.

Zephaniah is the precept to that: “Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee.” He is going to undo all the nations that afflict us. “and I will save her that halteth”: we are the ones that halt, because we are captive. “and gather her that was driven out.”

“and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.” We get that fame and that glory, and our children are going to get it too. Everybody is going to acknowledge who we are. “At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.”

That is the liberty proclaimed to the captives in Isaiah 61: not only freed, but honoured in the very lands that shamed us.

precepts.label: Isaiah 63:4
precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 proclaims “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to deliver his people. Isaiah 63 shows that day: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” This is Christ, the Son of God, and his garment is glorious, not a sheet or a robe.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah is asking Christ, Why are you red? It looks like you were stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod down the nations and killed them alone. He did not need the help of the twelve tribes of Israel; he did it himself.

“for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” The wine represents their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. The year of my redeemed is the acceptable year of the Lord in Isaiah 61, our jubilee, and it comes with the day of vengeance on the nations.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:41
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery. It is a different thing from the servant of Leviticus 25, a poor Hebrew brother who sold himself to his brother for six years and went out free and furnished in the year of release. Christianity used the words servants, obey your masters, to make us think the Bible's servant was chattel slavery; it is not. Deuteronomy 28:41 is the captivity that came as the curse.

It is what Jeremiah 34 brought on us. Zedekiah made all the people covenant to let every Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free, “that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” They obeyed, “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return”. This is some negro stuff: the elites among us, those who had money, wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude. So the Lord proclaimed a liberty for us “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, to be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That is Deuteronomy 28. Babylon had just left, and God brought them right back. That is the result of hating our brothers and not loving our neighbour as ourselves. Even after Persia set us free, in Nehemiah 5 the nobles did the same thing again.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek. 1 Maccabees 3:41: “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and “a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them.” We look at the slave auction and think it is the first time this ever happened. No, the Greeks did this too, and other nations helped them.

2 Maccabees 5 shows it: Jason, an Israelite, a treasonous negro, “slew his own citizens without mercy”, treating his countrymen like enemies to please the Greeks, and he died cast out, with none to mourn him. “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done” (Colossians 3:25). Then the king took the city: “fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” Apollonius was sent “to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort”. The best age, the movers and shakers who make a nation thrive; take them and leave the old and feeble, and you destroy the nation, the same complaint made about the colonialists.

So the sons and daughters we begat went into captivity, sold by the Greeks, and after them by Rome, whose foothold came when Pompey captured Jerusalem in 65 BC, and the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. That is where breaking the year of release led.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 23:13-16
precepts.why:
When Ezekiel dug in the wall, he saw “every form of creeping things, and abominable beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall round about.” That is like putting the images of Cesare Borgia on the walls, or Guadalupe on the walls, today. Ezekiel 23 shows what they were putting on the walls: images of the gods of their enemies.

“Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea”. Israel looked at the pictures of her enemies on the wall, dressed up like princes.

“And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” As soon as she saw them, she wanted them. That is why the Lord said in Numbers 15, when he gave us the fringes, that with your eyes you will go a whoring.

So the imagery on the walls of the temple in Ezekiel 8 was not harmless decoration. The images of other nations and their gods drew Israel's eyes, and her eyes drew her heart after them. It is the same today with the images hung on our walls, and it is why the Lord said, I cannot be around you all, and went far off from his sanctuary.

precepts.label: John 3:19
precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

precepts.label: Daniel 3:1-6
precepts.why:
Nebuchadnezzar is the head of gold in Daniel's dream, and before God humbled him in chapter 4, his pride is shown in chapter 3: “Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits: he set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon.” In his pride he set up a golden image and said everybody should worship it.

He gathered the princes, the governors, the captains, the judges and all the rulers of the provinces to its dedication, and “an herald cried aloud, To you it is commanded, O people, nations, and languages”, that when they heard the music they should “fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king hath set up”. And “whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.”

That is the same thing America does now with the flag. You don't bow down to it; now you have to stand up and salute it and honor it. It is the same as it was in ancient Babylon, just a different way.

This is why the decree of Daniel 4 came upon him. Nebuchadnezzar got prideful, and pride brings a man low. Twelve months after Daniel's interpretation he said, “Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?” God calls America Babylon the great, and Nebuchadnezzar called Babylon great himself. “While the word was in the king’s mouth”, the kingdom departed from him. You try to make people worship you, and it is taken.

He was made to eat grass as oxen “until thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men”. Until you humble yourself, you are eating grass. And he did humble himself; he came back and confessed there is no God like the God of Daniel. All kingdoms fall because of pride, Assyria, Babylon, the Greeks, Rome and America, and nobody is exempt from God's judgment for it.

classes.title: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:9
precepts.why:
Christ told Peter to forgive seventy times seven, and Christ never put numbers out just to put them there. Seven represents completion, but what is seventy times seven? Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”. That is 490 years, from Persia to Christ, “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

Who is the most Holy that is anointed? Hebrews 1:9 explains it: “Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.” That is talking about Christ. Where Daniel says “to anoint the most Holy”, that is Christ.

So the seventy weeks run “unto the Messiah the Prince”, which is Jesus Christ, and the reconciliation for iniquity and the end of sins come through him. The prophecy was 490 years, completing that perfection through Christ, because we needed that mercy. We couldn't sacrifice when we were enslaved under Babylon and Persia; we were always in captivity, going from one captivity to the next, so we needed Christ.

The apostles said it: “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel”. That is why he told Peter to forgive his brother seventy times seven: because he forgave us seventy times seven. He is that complete perfection. But don't take him for granted.

precepts.label: Luke 21:20
precepts.why:
“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”. That prince that shall come and destroy the sanctuary is Titus. “and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The flood is 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

Christ spoke of that same desolation: “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” What armies? The Roman armies. That is what Daniel 9:26 is speaking of, the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary.

Then Daniel 9:27: “in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation”. The Roman armies around Jerusalem were the sign that the desolation determined in the seventy weeks was at hand.

So the 490 years end with Christ cut off for us and the desolation of the city by Titus. After that there was no sacrifice for us but Christ, and that is why his sacrifice is our only way through to perfection.

precepts.label: Psalms 17:13
precepts.why:
Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

precepts.label: Isaiah 46:10
precepts.why:
Amos says “the Lord God of hosts is he that toucheth the land”. When Iran is being touched right now, and Israel, the Lord is involved in all of it; by his counsel the land gets touched. Isaiah shows that counsel: “Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done”.

This is the power we have: understanding that the Most High God from the very beginning planned every war, including the third world war to come. Ancient times means way back when Adam and Eve walked. From then he declared it. As his sons and daughters, the Israelites, we have to know our Father has this covered and his Son is coming back. Right now we have to rehearse the righteous acts and get right.

That is how we can make the bold statement that God is behind the Israelis doing what they do in the US government, and behind the Iranians spending twenty years building huge, elaborate tunnel systems and storing munitions and advanced rocketry. All of it was set up from ancient times. They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars, and the other side fires interceptor missiles that cost a million or more to take them out. You see how they will not be able to keep up. God put all that in these leaders.

“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure”. It was his pleasure when we went into chattel slavery, through Jim Crow and through civil rights. We had to learn the lesson.

Jeremiah shows the same counsel: “Therefore hear ye the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Babylon”. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: Israel, the least of Esau's flock, draws the United States out into the Middle East, and “At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth is moved”. Amos lived way before anything could melt the land. Today thermonuclear ICBMs can, and it is all by his counsel.

precepts.label: Luke 4:5-7
precepts.why:
Obadiah speaks “concerning Edom”: the white man, the Caucasian, by his biblical name. “Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”. They were so proud that they went to the moon and claimed it for their own, something they did not even create. They do not let other nations plant a flag there; they said, the Eagle has landed. And now one of their government says, we own the moon, why not Greenland? That is pride.

There is a reason behind it, and Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it. If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.”

This Edomite is prideful because he has the spiritual power of Satan rolling with him. That is who gave him the power to go to the moon and to make these weapons to destroy all of mankind. No brown nation on the earth came up with the invention to destroy everybody; that belongs solely to the white man, because Satan is behind him. That is who he made a covenant with, not the God of the Bible.

So when you see In God we trust on the money, know he is not talking about anybody in this Bible. The Psalm proves it: “The wicked, through the pride of his countenance, will not seek after God: God is not in all his thoughts.” “The wicked in his pride doth persecute the poor”, and you judge whether a man is prideful or humble by how he treats the lowly: the blacks, Hispanics and Native Indians, who have no army. Out of all the kingdoms, Assyrian, Babylonian, Persian, Greek, Roman, none has been more prideful than Esau.

But the kingdoms Satan gives are not the Lord's, and Obadiah answers the pride: “thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” From the moment they said the Eagle has landed, they have been going down, because that is when the Israelites started hitting the streets with the word of God. The more we are gathered together, the more Esau comes down.

precepts.label: Joshua 15:21
precepts.why:
Before Obadiah, the class read Jeremiah 50:19: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” To know whose land Carmel and Bashan were, go back to the first dividing of the land in Joshua. Write it down: Carmel was Judah's.

Joshua 15 gives the cities of Judah: “And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the coast of Edom southward were Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,” “And Kinah, and Dimonah”. Then jump to verse 55: “Maon, Carmel, and Ziph”. Those belonged to Judah. Judah's lot ran to the south, right up against the coast of Edom.

Jeremiah 50 goes on to say what God will do when he brings us back: “the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I reserve.” He wipes away our iniquity and brings us again to our own habitation.

Then watch how things get switched around. Obadiah says “they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau.” The mount of Esau is where Edom used to dwell originally, and we are going to take that whole area. “and they of the plain the Philistines”: we are going to take Palestine. We shall possess the fields of Ephraim and the fields of Samaria. The land is ours by inheritance from the first dividing, and when God brings Israel back it will be possessed even further than it was then.

precepts.label: Joshua 13:29
precepts.why:
Jeremiah 50:19 says Israel “shall feed on Carmel and Bashan”. Carmel was Judah's; now Bashan. Joshua 13 shows it: “And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.” “And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair”. Bashan belonged to Manasseh.

Read Jeremiah 50:19 again so you get the thought: “And I will bring Israel again to his habitation, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon mount Ephraim and Gilead.” God is bringing Israel back to the very lands the tribes were given at the beginning.

Now see how it gets switched around in Obadiah. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” Benjamin shall possess Gilead. The tribes come back to the land, but the land is shared out anew.

Verse 20 goes on: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”. The land of the Canaanites is the land of Israel, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Sepharad is the Asia Minor region and Spain. Our people scattered there come home and take the cities of the south.

precepts.label: Zechariah 10:10
precepts.why:
Obadiah said “Benjamin shall possess Gilead”, and Zechariah shows God bringing us there: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria; and I will bring them into the land of Gilead”. He is going to take us out of captivity and bring us into the land of Gilead. That is Obadiah 19 that was just read.

Then “and Lebanon”. Who belongs in Lebanon? Go back to Obadiah verse 20: “the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath”, and Zarephath is Lebanon. “and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.” Then verse 21: “And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau”, the mount of Edom.

Then “and place shall not be found for them.” There is not going to be enough room for us. Isaiah 49 says the same: “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. There will be too many of us. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the nations that swallowed us up shall be far away.

Then: “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” This place is too narrow; make room for me. That is why Christ said that in his Father's house are many mansions. Israel will come back in such numbers that the land cannot hold us.

precepts.label: Zechariah 13:8
precepts.why:
Isaiah 49:20 speaks of “The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”. The ones we lost are the two thirds, here in America. In case somebody asks what that means, Zechariah shows it: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord, two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein.”

Notice it says in all the land. The land it is talking about is Babylon, and that is America. So two out of every three Israelites shall die here in America. The ones we lost are them wicked Israelites.

Then the third: “And I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.”

That remnant is who goes back to possess the land in Obadiah. And even after the two thirds are gone, the children that are left shall say, “The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell.” The land will still be too narrow for the ones God brings back.

precepts.why:
Micah says, “Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction.” America, Babylon the great, all the lands we have been enslaved and colonised in, are not our rest. Isaiah shows why staying in them destroys us: “Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon”.

We despise God's word and trust in oppression. It was a sin for us to trust in this oppression and to stay and believe in it. “Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant.” There is no comfort and no protective covering in this society, in assimilating into America, Babylon the great. Our brothers and sisters that love this society and this world, it is our downfall as a people.

That is the pollution Micah speaks of. When you forget where you come from and get comfortable in the land of your captivity, it destroys you, because you begin to take on the attributes of your oppressor. That is not for us. We are God's children, and trying to make the oppressor's ways work for us always backfires. The white man has had the sword and the power to rule the world, but God will not let his children follow after him like the rest of the world and prosper.

So the wall breaks suddenly. In every place we have been, oppression, death and destruction follow behind us, and there is no peace there. Look at the families of Nolan Wales, of Kendrick Johnson, of the young woman found hanging from a tree in Mississippi: they never have rest again. And look at how we think as a people on social media and in all these podcasts: from the aged man and aged woman down to the children, we are in a sore destruction, because we have gotten comfortable in our captivity, “forgotten their restingplace”, and do not even want to go back to our homeland.

precepts.label: John 1:29
precepts.why:
We did not return to what the Most High commanded, the feasts he told us to go back to, and that is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. From Abraham to David, from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and from Babylon to Christ were fourteen generations each; we were always in slavery.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His name means he saves. His people: the Israelites only. From their sins. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” The Lamb of God. Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice, the lamb that takes away the sins of the people he came to save.

precepts.label: Hebrews 10:5-8
precepts.why:
To expound further on Christ being the ultimate sacrifice: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. The body was Christ. The sacrificial laws of animal sacrifice were a preparation for what was to come, a shadow of good things to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ, dying only for the nation of Israel.

“In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in those sacrifices. They were temporary, to train us and prepare us for Christ.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” In the volume of the book: the whole book, not just the New Testament. Christ is present in the Old Testament, and Christ is present before the Old Testament.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. So the offerings of the law pointed to the body prepared for him, the one sacrifice that saves his people from their sins.

precepts.label: John 1:3
precepts.why:
Christ was always the plan. He is the author, the executive producer, whatever title you want to give him. From before the Old Testament, the body prepared for him in the volume of the book was the plan for saving his people from their sins.

John shows it: “All things were made by him”. All things were made by Christ: the principalities, the things you see out in space, the worlds, with an s. “And without him was not any thing made that was made.”

The one who made all things is the one who came as the Lamb of God to save his people. The sacrifices of the law, the seventh day and the rest it points to were all his from the beginning. So when the angel said “thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins”, it was the Maker of all things coming to fulfil the plan that was always his.

precepts.label: Luke 17:3-4
precepts.why:
Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance, the perpetual hatred Esau carries against his brother Jacob. Now the flip side: Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” Christ answered, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ offers boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to do the same.

Luke gives the terms: “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.” That brother is the children of thy people, as Leviticus 19:17 says. It is rebuke first, then repentance, then forgiveness.

“And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.” Why? Seven represents completion. The same way Christ forgave us when we were without sacrifice and without mercy: all our adulteries, fornication, lying and stealing during Assyria, Babylon, Persia and America, scattered in Africa in the dark ages doing all sorts of wicked things. Christ forgave all of that. That is why he said seventy times seven.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:12-13
precepts.why:
“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness”, the mercy Christ offers us, “humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”: longsuffering toward the brother who repents. “Forbearing one another”, as Christ forbears us, “and forgiving one another”.

Forgiving is something some of us need to pray for. Some can forgive nothing and hold on to grudges like there is no tomorrow. Imagine if Christ held on to grudges against us. We would not be here; we would be in hell with white Jesus, Islam and our sins. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ and his boundless mercy toward us.

“If any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” Christ does not put numbers out just to put them. Seventy times seven is 490, and Daniel's seventy weeks, 490 years from Persia to Christ, were determined “to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity” through the Messiah cut off for the children of Israel. We could not sacrifice in Babylon and Persia; we needed Christ, the complete perfection of mercy. He forgave us seventy times seven, so we forgive our brother the same, and we do not take him for granted.

classes.title: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18-20
precepts.why:
Paul says “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly”. If God is revealing himself to you, and he doesn't deal with everybody, you had better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God.

Solomon shows why: “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” We are all beasts. Although we may be the sons and daughters of God, at the same time we are still beasts in his eyes.

“For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other”. The lion, the bug that has no value in the eyes of God and just serves the purpose it was created for: we die just like them. “yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.” This is Solomon, the wisest man ever to walk the earth besides Jesus the Christ, saying you have no preeminence above a beast.

So who are you to think you are better than that, to reject what God has written and do as thou wilt? Break it down to its lowest form, and we perish just like everything else. That is where humbleness comes in. We came here and we are going to leave here, so apply these excellent things to your life before you go back to your Maker.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6-7
precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

precepts.label: Psalms 90:10
precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

precepts.label: Sirach 14:17-19
precepts.why:
“All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, Thou shalt die the death.” That is what we just read in David: seventy, maybe eighty years. That is the covenant God pronounced from the beginning: thou shalt die the death.

“As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one cometh to an end, and another is born.” That is why we have kids. You watch them grow up, and you say, man, I'm getting old. You know the covenant God pronounced upon all flesh, and you are about to cross it too.

“Every work rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker thereof shall go withal.” That is the covenant: thou shalt die the death, thus saith the Lord. Everything a man builds goes with him. So there is no room to think of yourself more highly than you ought; think soberly, knowing the covenant is coming for you like every other leaf on the tree.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
Why do we die? We try to break it down so the new people coming into the faith can put the puzzle together: “For the wages of sin is death”. That is why the covenant, thou shalt die the death, passed upon all of us. When Adam listened to his wife Eve and consented to the idolatry she brought to him, sin came into the world, and when sin came, death came with it.

“but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That is what we get in the repentance. But we still have to go through the covenant of all flesh. You can't receive the gift of eternal life while you are still in the flesh; flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of heaven. We have to pass through that covenant.

And one thing we had better make sure we don't have on us when we leave this body is pride. That will keep us out of it for sure. That is why Paul says not to think of yourself more highly than you ought: the one who dies like the beasts receives the gift only through Christ, and only if he goes to his grave humble.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:4-9
precepts.why:
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. That baptism is Moses teaching us the laws of God, and teaching us the gospel, teaching us about Christ, because Moses spoke with Christ. Christ said, “Before Abraham was, I am”: it was Christ that spoke directly to Moses. We often think the gospel only begins in the book of Matthew. It does not.

Ezra shows it: “And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”. That mount is Sinai, and the long season is the forty days and forty nights. “And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

Moses was shown the beginning, the middle and the end of times; that is how he was able to write about it in the first five books. He even saw himself not entering the promised land. “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

“That thou lay up in thy heart the signs that I have shewed, and the dreams that thou hast seen, and the interpretations which thou hast heard: For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.”

So when Paul says our fathers “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ”, it is plain: the Israelites in the wilderness were taught the gospel through Moses, who had been with Christ on the mount. Those things are written “for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”; we learn from our forefathers the same way the congregations scattered in Asia Minor did, and the acts of the apostles continue.

precepts.label: Psalms 18:20-23
precepts.why:
Paul forgives “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” So examine yourself: has Satan been using some form of pride to hold you back and keep you down? It may be subtle: not asking for help, thinking too highly of yourself, I'm good, I'm fine. Satan has many devices and can transform himself into an angel of light. Captain Matthew put it plainly: fat brothers are too prideful, and that is why they won't change their eating habits.

David shows the other way. “The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me. For I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God. For all his judgments were before me, and I did not put away his statutes from me.” We all know David committed adultery and put out a hit on a brother. So what does it mean that he did not put away his statutes?

When Nathan the prophet brought it to him, he said, that's me. God was going to take away the child; he fasted and prayed, and when it happened he washed his face, ate bread and said it was the Lord's judgment. He was not prideful. He did not say, I'm the king, I can have as many women as I want, God chose me. He acknowledged his sin, humbled himself and did not put the judgments away.

“I was also upright before him, and I kept myself from mine iniquity.” He went on forward and walked in the ways of the Lord, to the point where God said David is a man after my own heart, because he humbled himself when his sins were brought to him. That is how you keep Satan from getting an advantage of you.

precepts.label: Proverbs 29:23
precepts.why:
Look what pride does: “A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.” Pride is one of Satan's devices, and it does not have to be loud and in your face. It can be subtle. Sometimes it shuts you down, I can do this on my own, I don't need anybody, and it always points the finger at somebody else and never at yourself. Pride destroyed us in the kingdom, and it can keep destroying us right now.

Pride destroyed every kingdom on the earth. The king of Assyria sent his messenger with big words against Hezekiah and the Lord, and the angel of the Lord smote a hundred fourscore and five thousand in one night; then his own sons killed Sennacherib with the sword while he worshipped his god. Nebuchadnezzar said, is not this great Babylon, built by the might of my power, and while the word was in his mouth the kingdom departed from him, and he ate grass as oxen until he knew that the Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men. Antiochus spoke proudly and was smitten with a remedyless pain of the bowels. Herod took the glory of a god and was eaten of worms.

No kingdom is exempt, not Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome or America. And none is more prideful than Edom, the white man, of whom it is written, the pride of thine heart hath deceived thee.

But honour upholds the humble in spirit. Nebuchadnezzar humbled himself and came back saying there is no God like the God of Daniel. David humbled himself and God called him a man after his own heart. The only way our kingdom will last forever is to walk in wisdom and humility towards God; outside of that, pride brings us low like every nation before us.
