precepts.label: Romans 7:14
precepts.why:
“Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” What is the Spirit you have to walk in so that you never do amiss? “For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” The law is spiritual. We are carnal, sold under sin. So if we want to stop being carnal and stop sinning, we have to keep the law.

That is what walking in the Spirit means: walking in the ordinances, the laws, the statutes and the commandments of the Lord God. If you are doing these things, you are never going to do amiss.

“For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”. There is a war within you. The old man always wants to be around, in your business: reading the Bible? You don't need to read the Bible. Let's go rob a house, steal a car, boost cars like you used to, call your man for two birds, go fly some kites. The only way you win this war is by actually reading your Bible and applying what you read.

If you do not read, pray or fast, miss all the new moons and feast days, and show up on the Sabbath just to keep up appearances, you will not be able to fight the lust within your flesh, because you are not walking in the Spirit. The flesh will always be present; it is what you put in you now that fights it. So stay in this book, the spiritual law, and the carnal man is subdued.

precepts.label: John 6:63
precepts.why:
“It is the spirit that quickeneth”: only the spirit can change you as a man. “the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” So when Galatians says walk in the Spirit, it means walk in the words of Christ, the laws, statutes and commandments, and you will not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

Those words have to live in you. The Bible should be like the receptionist at the front desk of an office building: nobody gets in unless she lets them. The door to your soul is your forehead, so the Bible should sit there. When the plan comes up, it says, I hear you, but that's two to five; that's ten to fifteen; that's life. Thou shalt not steal.

When you see a beautiful woman and are tempted to start rubbernecking, you remember Job: I made a covenant with my eyes, why then should I think upon a maid? If you walk in a place and there's a stack of money with nobody around, thou shalt not steal. Without the scriptures readily in your mind, it is impossible not to fall into temptation.

And hidden wickedness does not stay hidden. We are not small any more. A brother making a delivery from another state was recognized by someone not even in the truth. Imagine if he had been doing wickedness. The words of Christ are spirit and life; the flesh profits nothing.

classes.title: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.label: Colossians 3:22
precepts.why:
“Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh”. These are the same scriptures Esau uses to justify slavery, and that dumb black people use to reject the Bible. But it is not talking about chattel slavery. It is what was read in Leviticus 25 and Exodus: Israel, in a time of stability, still following the laws on selling yourself to work if you were poor or owed debts.

Leviticus says it: “And if thy brother that dwelleth by thee be waxen poor, and be sold unto thee; thou shalt not compel him to serve as a bondservant: But as an hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be with thee, and shall serve thee unto the year of jubile”. Then he departs, he and his children, back to his own family, because “Thou shalt not rule over him with rigour”. Rigour is chattel slavery, and God forbade it over a brother.

Colossians says the same: “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. The servants were Israelites, Hebrew servants, hired servants.

Exodus 21 shows the master: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.” If his master gave him a wife and she bore children, he could say, “I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free”. Why would he say, I love my master? Because the brother treated him real good. That is what “Servants, obey in all things your masters” is talking about.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 2:18
precepts.why:
“Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear; not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward.” This is in the slave Bible; Esau used it. But the good and gentle masters and the froward ones were Israelite masters. The law said not to deal with Israel with rigour, meaning hard, yet some of them were like that. The froward ones are the ones who did not really like you.

“For this is thankworthy, if a man for conscience toward God endure grief, suffering wrongfully. For what glory is it, if, when ye be buffeted for your faults, ye shall take it patiently? but if, when ye do well, and suffer for it, ye take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.”

Why would a master not like his servant? Exodus 22: a thief found breaking in, “If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be blood shed for him; for he should make full restitution; if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.” That is different from a poor brother saying, I lack food, clothing and shelter, will you help me? If I broke into your house, stole all your stuff and got caught, now I have to work for you, and you are not going to like me too much. You have to see him every morning.

So Peter tells servants to be subject even to the froward master, and to take it patiently. It is Israelite servitude under the law, not chattel slavery.

precepts.label: Titus 2:9
precepts.why:
“Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again”: not talking back. Esau perverted this. But read on: “Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.” To purloin is to steal something: sticky fingers, a kleptomaniac. That is what was read in Exodus 22. Paul is dealing with brothers who were stealing, got caught, and were sold to make restitution.

Philemon shows it plainly. Paul met Onesimus while under arrest. He had been a servant to Philemon, and he ran away: “For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved”. Deal with him like a brother beloved.

Was he a servant because he was poor, or because he did something bad? “If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account”. He owed something because he stole or broke something, and Paul said, put it on my account.

So Paul was dealing with servants who were Hebrews, Israelites in servitude to other Israelites. Chattel slavery came later, when Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, under Rome, Spain and Portugal, France, Britain and the United States.

precepts.label: Galatians 1:6
precepts.why:
How did “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters” become a scripture used to justify chattel slavery? This is what they did: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another; but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.”

That is what Esau did. They took this Bible and perverted it. The servants of Ephesians, Colossians, Peter and Titus were Israelites serving Israelites under the law, hired servants and sojourners who went free in the seventh year and at the jubilee, and whom God said not to rule with rigour. Esau took those scriptures and made them into the slave Bible, to justify ruling over us with rigour in chattel slavery.

And dumb black people, seeing how Esau used them, reject the Bible altogether, not knowing it was perverted.

But God says, “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee”. He gave Egypt for our ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for us, because we are precious in his sight, and he will give men for us. He will bring our seed from the east and gather us from the west, say to the north, give up, and deliver us into the glorious liberty of the children of God. That is the true jubilee.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 8:52
precepts.why:
“For we which have believed do enter into rest.” What is that rest that is promised? Ezra shows it: “For unto you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted, the time to come is prepared, plenteousness is made ready, a city is builded, and rest is allowed, yea, perfect goodness and wisdom.”

This paradise is spoken to the Israelites. It is not talking about all nations. Paradise opened, the tree of life planted, a city builded and rest allowed: that is what is left to us, the promise “of entering into his rest.”

“For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them.” The gospel did not begin in the book of Matthew; Christ was taught to our forefathers too. But “the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” They disobeyed Christ and were moved with unbelief, and their unbelief is what kept them from entering in. “Let us therefore fear”, then, lest any of us come short of the paradise and the rest that is allowed to Israel.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 3:5-6
precepts.why:
Paul says God’s works “were finished from the foundation of the world.” The rest is not something new; it was prepared before anything else was. Ezra shows it: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was here before the earth came forth. Before Christ said the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here. That is the paradise opened to Israel in 2 Esdras 8:52, where the tree of life is planted and rest is allowed.

So when Hebrews says the works were finished from the foundation of the world, it is telling you the rest was already created and waiting. Then “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” That number seven keeps coming back: the seventh day Sabbath points to that rest God prepared from the beginning.

precepts.label: Micah 4:10
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Paul is making a comparison between our works and God’s. God worked, then rested; so must we. Micah shows the labour: “Be in pain, and labour to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail: for now shalt thou go forth out of the city.”

No matter what we are going through, brothers and sisters, we have to be in pain and do this work. Be in pain to bring forth the kingdom of heaven on earth.

That is why Paul says “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” Labour, labour in pain, bring forth your works to enter into that rest, which is the kingdom. Rest is entered by labour. The generation in the wilderness fell because of unbelief; the daughter of Zion must travail to bring forth.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:13
precepts.why:
“For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.” Revelation shows who rests and why: “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.”

They rest from their labours, and their works follow them. Your works are what are going to allow you to enter in through those gates. The rest is not handed to the idle; it comes after the labour, and the labour goes with you into it.

So “Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief” that we read of in the wilderness. Labour in pain, bring forth your works, like the daughter of Zion in travail, and then rest from those labours in the kingdom.

precepts.label: Isaiah 14:1-3
precepts.why:
The seventh day Sabbath, resting from our servile work, is a similitude the Most High uses for us resting in the kingdom when it is established. That is the true rest, when we will really rest from servile work. Because after the Sabbath some of us have to go to work on Sunday, then Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, slaving for Esau.

Isaiah shows the day of that rest: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob.” The nations are going to be joined with us, but how? “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” They are our possession.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve.” That is the true rest: rest from our sorrow, from our fear, and from the hard bondage we were made to serve.

That is why “if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.” That Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the Hamites, but we did not get true rest in the land; there were enemies on all sides, the Amalekites and the Hamites we were fighting. The true rest is the kingdom of God on earth, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.”

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:7-8
precepts.why:
“And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Peter shows how that seventh day reaches forward to the kingdom: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years. So the seventh day is not only the Sabbath we keep each week; it maps to a thousand years, the reign that comes after the heavens and earth that are now are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

That is why “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest of the seventh day is the similitude, and the thousand years is the substance: the day we reign with Christ, as Revelation 20:4 shows.

precepts.label: Revelation 20:4
precepts.why:
If one day with the Lord is a thousand years, what is the seventh day rest? Revelation shows it: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.”

They lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. That is going into the rest. The seventh day Sabbath represents us resting with Christ, and every seventh day is rehearsing it.

The rest promised in Hebrews is not the land Joshua brought us into, and not only the one day a week before going back to labour in Esau’s system. It is the eternal reign with Christ when he comes back, sitting on thrones with judgment given to us, rulership over our enemies. “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” Seven represents completion, and the seventh day points to that completion: the kingdom and the thousand years with Christ.

precepts.label: Matthew 5:37
precepts.why:
“let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.” When you say yes, I am going to do it, do it. When you say no, you can’t, then don’t. But never say yes, get paid to do the job, and then not do it. Christ put it this way: “But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.”

You are evil when you lie to your brothers. Anything other than yea and nay is evil, and if you are evil you are going to be condemned: not by us, but by the Lord. Condemn means to declare reprehensible, wrong or evil, usually after weighing evidence. The Lord is going to review your case like a court docket: the state versus so-and-so, how do you plead, not guilty, bring the witness. He didn’t know they had the witnesses.

The eyes of the Lord are in every place, beholding the evil and the good, and he rewards every man according to his deeds. Curse not the king in your chamber, lest a bird carry the news. You do evil in a different state with somebody we never met, and another brother goes to that state for a job and meets the same person. After a joyful Sabbath together, two brothers got in the car, one pocket-dialed the captain, and he heard them talking trash about all the ranking men. When questioned, the first thing was a lie.

When people bring up your evil without anybody asking one question, the Lord is exposing you because he wants you to get right. He could have let you do it to the wrong person, and we find out at your funeral: he stole a hundred grand and a dude put two in his back. You can sit home and hate the messenger, or recognize the mistake, apologize, make amends and walk in the spirit so blessing comes your way. The choice is yours.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:9
precepts.why:
“Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds.” It is forbidden for us to lie one to another. We must be men of character, men of honour, because the world must look at us and say, surely this is a wise and understanding people. If you are lying, how is the world going to say that? They will say this is an evil-ass negro, and the truth gets evil spoken of, because the whole time you were doing it you had fringes on your clothes.

At no time did you look down at your fringes and say, damn, I can’t behave this way, I can’t do this to my brother, not even to people in the world. Why? Because you are not in the Bible. There is no way you are in the Bible and doing evil at the same time; it is an oxymoron. You just finished reading thou shalt not steal, I love that scripture, let me get my gun? It doesn’t go that way. The word has to be nowhere near your head for you to go do evil. That is why you stay in this Bible and give attendance to reading, continuously, so the word is in you.

A bishop “must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.” People in the world will lie on us, but they should never be able to back it up. In business in the world you must be twice as honourable, and you will get more jobs, because nobody likes a thief. Penny wise, pound foolish: make an extra penny now and lose the whole pound. Lie and steal, and you end up ducking people, circling the block, getting beaten over twenty dollars, and still owing the money. The devil convinced you it was okay to lie, then removed himself. Put off the old man and his deeds, and lie not one to another.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:36
precepts.why:
“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the way of knowledge is the Bible. The Bible does not belong to all nations on earth; it was given only to the beloved Israelites.

That is who Peter is writing to: “This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you”, to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance, “That ye may be mindful of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets”. The beloved of 2 Peter 3 is Israel his beloved of Baruch, the ones the way of knowledge was given to.

So when Peter warns “that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts”, he is warning the beloved about scoffers among them. Are we not seeing scoffers in these last days, like never before? Every black urban apologist is a scoffer. They don't believe the Bible. They don't believe Christ is black. They think Jesus is Caesar Borgia and the white man is coming to deliver them.

They say “Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.” Nothing has changed. But they “willingly are ignorant”, because we can take them to Deuteronomy and show them how things were prophesied and have come to pass, and it fits us perfect to a T. How are you going to say the Bible isn't a true book, when the knowledge in it was given to you?

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 2:2
precepts.why:
Peter asks, since this whole earth is reserved unto fire, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”. That means we have to act right and speak right. A lot of our conversation is filth and sports. We have to train ourselves to speak the words of this book.

When we came into the school, they used to say about one of the elders: if you weren't talking about the Bible, don't talk to him; that's all he wanted to hear. Paul said the same: “For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” He trained himself. All I want to hear is Bible. I don't want to hear Betty got a big booty. I don't want to hear how many touchdowns somebody ran or how far he hit the jump shot. I don't want to hear that crap.

That is holy conversation, and godliness is our actions, our works: the way we live must match the way we speak. The scoffers walk after their own lusts and their conversation follows their lusts. The beloved, knowing the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, train their minds and spirits to know nothing but Christ and him crucified, so that they may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

precepts.label: Isaiah 60:21
precepts.why:
Peter says “we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.” Isaiah 60 shows what that promise is. “Violence shall no more be heard in thy land”: the white man will be subdued, because he is the violent man, behind every coup and every war. The land is the land of Israel, with no “wasting nor destruction within thy borders”, and “thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise.”

“The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light”. That doesn't mean the sun and moon are done away with; they will be there, but the Israelites won't need them, because the Lord will be our light. “Thy sun shall no more go down”: our understanding shall no more go down, and our moon, our understanding, won't withdraw itself. And “the days of thy mourning shall be ended.”

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever”. That is why the new earth is one wherein dwelleth righteousness: because our people shall be all righteous. Esau isn't going to be there enjoying anything. “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation”: we're going to have a whole lot of children. “I the Lord will hasten it in his time”: I'm going to speed it up.

The scoffers say all things continue as they were. But one day is with the Lord as a thousand years; he is not slack concerning his promise. So, beloved, seeing we look for such things, be diligent to be found of him in peace, without sin, and blameless.

thread.text: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

precepts.label: Baruch 4:25
precepts.why:
Peter says “that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” David says our days are seventy, eighty years. Do the math: if a thousand years is one day to God, eighty years is 0.08 of a day, about an hour and fifty-five minutes. An entire human lifetime is less than two hours to God, and it may be even less than that; the concept of time does not apply to the Ancient of days. Eighty years and you come back and God says, you just left, why you back already?

That is why the scriptures say things like Baruch: “My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee”. It is happening right now. We are going through it, and it seems like forever, because down here it takes forever to become an adult, to get your license, to turn 21. Lord, come save us; they are doing their worst.

Then, “but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” Shortly: in less than a few minutes of God's time your life is over, and in an hour or so you see the destruction of your enemy and have a lifetime of God time, eternal. So suffer patiently. What seems long to us is short to him.

precepts.label: Isaiah 54:7-8
precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” A small moment. That is why God says small moment: it is not even two hours to him, not even a day to him. If a thousand years is as one day with the Lord, our whole captivity is a moment in his eyes.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.” For a moment. Start thinking like that: I'm only here for a short while.

And since it is only a moment, Peter gives the wisdom Christ put in his mouth: “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time”. The real exaltation we want is when we go back to him: a crown from God Almighty, and you can't get any higher than that. “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He knows you only have a short amount of time here.

Right after that comes “your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”, because Satan is looking for the prideful, the ones who think they know more than God in the little time they have been here. We stress over three to five business days and get mad when Amazon doesn't deliver in two. God's small moment calls for humility, not pride.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 3:5
precepts.why:
We feel what we are going through. We complain, we cry, we fast, we do what we can to make it through. But look what God calls it: “And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. A little chastised. We are not even yet at the point of being persecuted and put to death, and he calls this a little chastising.

That fits with 2 Peter 3:8: if one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, a whole lifetime of suffering is a little chastising, less than two hours in his eyes, and the reward that follows is eternal.

Then, “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The chastising is the proving. He tries us to find us worthy unto himself. So we have to endure to the end, people. We have to endure to the end, humbling ourselves under his mighty hand, and when the short moment is over, those found worthy will be greatly rewarded.

“All they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” If you want life, if you don’t want your light put out, you keep the commandments: read the Bible, learn the laws, statutes and commandments, and apply them. You tell me, do you want life or death? Being here shows you want life; the question is whether you will do what it takes, or revert to the old man and give in to your lust.

“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” Why is his vesture dipped in blood? Because Christ is about righteous destruction; you read that in Isaiah 63. The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God, and a merciful one, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle.

How do we know this is Jesus? Revelation 1:1: “The Revelation of Jesus Christ”. The whole book is the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. So the rider of Revelation 19, with eyes as a flame of fire, is Jesus Christ, and when he comes back he is not going to meet them as a man.

That is our hope: to see it and be part of it, the kingdom where all the wrongs done to us get turned upside down and right is instilled in the earth. Not a pie-in-the-sky fairy tale from modern-day Christianity, but Christ coming back to make war.

precepts.label: Revelation 1:14-15

Why his feet like fine brass, as if burned in a furnace? Because you cannot deny it anymore: Jesus Christ was a black man. The Bible says it first and foremost, and there is archaeological proof and historical evidence besides. Everyone knows it except the dumb Americans here in this country, and I say that because I was a dumb American; we were all dumb at one point. A lot of Eastern Europeans know Jesus was black. Vladimir Putin knows Jesus was black.

So this is who is coming: the black Christ whose eyes are like a flame of fire, his vesture dipped in blood. Jesus Christ is coming back to make war. Understand that now, as the wars are here and God is orchestrating every one of them from the beginning.

Assyrian, Babylon, Greek, Rome, America: nobody is exempt from pride and God destroying them.

The same judgment is on us. The power God gave was given to us by God too, and for our pride as a nation we have been destroyed. Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

precepts.label: Psalms 100:3
precepts.why:
“Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.” Pride, arrogance, disdain, the inability to admit fault, the inflated ego: God said it wasn't made for you. You are nothing but dust that shall return to where it came from. And anger doesn't get you anywhere either; it holds you back and stunts your growth.

Why wasn't pride made for us? “Know ye that the Lord he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves”. You didn't put one finger on your hand. You didn't put the knee bone with the hip bone and the leg bone. All of that belongs to God, the Creator, from way back when he said, Let us make man in our image.

He didn't consult you: where should I put the knee? How high up on the leg should it go? What should the arch of the foot look like? What skin tone should I give them? What should I make their hair like? None of us were included in that conversation.

So pride has no ground to stand on. The one who did not make himself cannot be proud before the one who made him. That is why the beginning of pride is turning away from your Maker.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 11:5
precepts.why:
“As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit”: you don't know how the spirit was even made, and the body doesn't function without a spirit in it. We say someone is soulless, and it may be jacked up and crooked like the Esau in them, but that body isn't walking around with nothing in it. This is not a movie where they clone you and you come back with no soul, or a vampire who lives forever and can't see his reflection. There is a spirit in all of us, and the Most High made that.

“nor how the bones do grow in the womb of her that is with child”. Science tries to explain it the best way it can, by the mitochondria and this and that, but they don't know what God did to make it. Science is God giving man some sense of his mastery, and man takes it and says, I can do better than God: let me put this rod on you as a woman, let me cut yours off. That's why the Bible warns us to beware of science that opposes God.

“even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.” So why is earth and ashes proud? Man does not even know how he himself was made; pride was not made for men.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:7
precepts.why:
Solomon mentions that spirit again: “Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

The body goes back to the dust it came from, and the spirit goes back to God who made it. All of this, the dust and the spirit, belongs to the Most High God. That is why pride is not made for us.

Sirach asks, “Why is earth and ashes proud?” and says that when a man is dead “he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.” The man who is today a king tomorrow shall die. Neither the body nor the spirit is ours to boast in: one returns to the earth, the other to its Maker. So the beginning of pride, departing from God and turning the heart away from the Maker, is turning away from the very one the spirit must return to.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 6:20
precepts.why:
“For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” That is who your body belongs to.

This isn't something the young ones usually fight with. It's us, as we get older, who start smelling ourselves: I'm going to do this, this is what I want to do. We forget that at the end of the day we are still the children of the Most High God. You don't get to tell him what you are going to do with that body. The way parents look at their son and say, you'll always be my baby, even at forty-seven with gray hair: apply that to your life with God.

You have to keep these commandments, because he is still your Father and that is what he said to do. And that is the beginning of pride in Sirach 10: “when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” As we get older we start thinking we can decide whether to serve God or obey our Father, and that is pride. Pride is the beginning of sin; don't tell yourself you have a good heart while you depart from his commandments. Pride is hateful before God, and what he hates has an expiration date.

Under the Greeks, “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and Syria and the Philistines joined in. Others helped the Greeks, and so did one of our own.

We think our people love themselves; no. He treated us like enemies, because he wanted to please the Greeks. Don't be surprised when you see black men and black women do all they can to please the enemies of our people. They will be worse on you than white men.

Read on: “for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason”. He was a treasonous negro, and the Most High cannot stand a traitor. He was “fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen”, and “cast out into Egypt.” Imagine being banished, unable to come back to your own country because you were a traitor.

“Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land”, thinking to find succour among the Lacedemonians, where Sparta was. “And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.” What goes around comes around.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:25
precepts.why:
Jason drove many out of their country and perished in a strange land; he cast out many unburied and had none to mourn for him. That is the law Paul states: “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons.”

Negroes do evil and think there is not going to be a big payback. You are going to get it. It does not matter that Jason was an Israelite; there is no respect of persons. He slew his own citizens without mercy to please the Greeks, and he received shame for the reward of his treason.

And it was not only Jason. When the king heard of it, he thought Judea had revolted, took the city by force of arms, and there was “killing of young and old”, fourscore thousand destroyed in three days, and no fewer sold as slaves than slain. The Greeks were selling us as slaves long before the slave auctions we know today, and the ones among us who help the enemy against our own people will receive for the wrong they have done.

precepts.label: Psalms 96:5
precepts.why:
The third brother, when they came to cut him, put out his tongue right away and held forth his hands manfully: come on, let's get this over with. He said courageously, “These I had from heaven; and for his laws I despise them; and from him I hope to receive them again.” And “the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man's courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

Why did they marvel? They had to understand there was a certain spirit in these brothers; there was something the brothers knew that the king did not. The psalm tells what it is: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

All the gods of the nations are idols, so the nations have no living God. The king had power, arrogance and the fire, but his gods were dead. These brothers served the Lord that made the heavens, the God who gave them their tongues and hands and would give them again. That is why they were ready to die rather than transgress the laws of their fathers, and why the heathen could only stand there and marvel.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 8:5-6
precepts.why:
The king marveled at the young man's courage, and Paul shows the reason. “For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,) But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.”

Because we understand that there is only one living God, that is why they marvel. That is why the king was marveling. The nations have gods many and lords many, but a man who knows the one God, the Father, and the one Lord Jesus Christ can say, “we are ready to die, rather than to transgress the laws of our fathers.”

Do you know what level of faith that is? You truly cannot desire anything left in this world. We are already captives: you have bills, you work fourteen hours a day. What are you leaving? There has to be something better. So the brothers went to the fire expecting “the King of the world” to raise them up “unto everlasting life”, and the fourth told the king, “as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.”

That hope belongs to those who have the one God. What kind of mercy would it be for the same people that torment us to get an equal reward in the kingdom? That is not a merciful God. The one God of Israel will of his own mercy give his servants breath and life again.

precepts.why:
Cyrus the Persian humbled himself and let all Israel go, and God said, you can rule. But the Greek Antiochus “had spoken proudly”, saying “he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” As soon as he spoke those proud words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”, and that most justly, because he had tormented other men’s bowels. He fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and finally said “It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God.”

It did not stop with the Greeks. Now we come down to the Romans, because that is what Herod was: “And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.”

Black folk always think the white man is God, and God always has to remind you who he is. “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Antiochus rotted with worms rising out of his body; Herod was eaten of worms. The same judgment for the same pride.

Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America. That is the judgment for it. So check yourself before you wreck yourself: a man that is mortal must not think of himself as if he were God.
